entries.justification: The two iframe elements at cadres-html/dom.html:27 and 31 have empty title attributes (title=""). Test 2.2.1 asks whether 'le contenu de cet attribut title' (the content of the title attribute) is pertinent for each frame having a title attribute. Since these frames have no title content, there is no title to judge for pertinence. The pertinence judgment criterion presupposes the existence of a title, which is not present here. This criterion is not applicable when the prerequisite condition (presence of a title) is not met.

Examination of the rendered page and source code reveals no instances where information is conveyed uniquely by color. Text elements use color for styling hierarchy (gray text for secondary content) but the information content is in the text itself, not dependent on the color. Links are identified by both blue color and underline. The colored elements do not transmit information that would be lost if color were removed. Tests 3.1.1-3.1.6 require alternatives for information given 'uniquement par la couleur' (solely by color), but no such color-only information conveyance exists in this scope.

Multiple text elements throughout the site exhibit contrast ratios well below the RGAA 3.2 thresholds. Normal text (<24px) requires 4.5:1 (test 3.2.1), and larger text (≥24px) requires 3:1 (test 3.2.3). Measured ratios include 1.92:1, 2.38:1, and 2.85:1, all failing to meet either threshold. No contrast-adjustment mechanism is provided to users. The evidence shows this pattern across multiple pages (accueil, cadres-html, contact-html, documents-html, medias-html, mentions-legales-html, plan-html, recherche-html, tarifs-html).

This affects the accueil and contact-html pages particularly, making form fields visually indistinguishable from the page background.

entries.justification: L'analyse des éléments sémantiques (h1, h2, h3, h4, ul, li, nav, table, form, etc.) montre qu'ils sont utilisés de manière conforme à leur sémantique. Les tableaux de données sont correctement structurés, les listes contiennent du contenu pertinent, les éléments de navigation sont marqués de façons appropriées. La seule table avec role="presentation" (ligne 87 de tarifs-html) est correctement marquée pour indiquer une utilisation purement présentationnelle, ce qui est permis par le test 8.9.1.

entries.justification: The plan.html page violates 9.1.1 by having a heading hierarchy skip (h4 after h1), and violates 9.1.2 by containing an empty h2 heading. Both violations are confirmed in the DOM source at the cited locations.

findings.message: Heading level skip detected: h4 follows h1 without intermediate h2/h3 levels. The heading hierarchy jumps from level 1 to level 4, violating pertinent hierarchy.
Empty heading: h2 element contains no text content, which disoriients keyboard and screen reader navigation.

entries.justification: The document structure violates 9.2.1 in three ways: (1) accueil has navigation links in header without <nav> element, (2) documents-html lacks <main> element entirely, and (3) plan-html contains multiple visible <main> elements without proper visibility management. These are structural violations confirmed in the DOM.

findings.message: Navigation links present in header (lines 19-27) but no <nav> element or role="navigation" attribute to structure them as navigation. The 9 navigation links are in a header without proper navigation landmark.
Main content lacks <main> element. The h1 and subsequent content (lines 22-36) appear directly in body without <main> landmark, failing to identify the primary content area.
Multiple <main> elements present (at lines 22 and 57). Only one main content area should be visible; the second main at line 57 should have hidden attribute or appropriate visibility control.

entries.justification: The plan.html page violates 9.3.1 by containing a non-<li> element (<span>) as a direct child of <ul>. Unordered lists must use proper <ul>/<li> structure or WAI-ARIA role="list"/role="listitem" attributes.

findings.message: List structure violation: <span> element at line 47 is a direct child of <ul> but is not wrapped in <li>. Only <li> elements should be direct children of <ul>.

entries.justification: No quotations (neither short quotations using <q> nor block quotations using <blockquote>) were found in the audited scope. The evidence lists 59 distinct content classes including headings, lists, tables, and form elements, but no actual citations or quotations. Since the criterion's subject (quotations to be marked up) does not exist in the audited scope, the criterion is not applicable.

The visible information present in the rendered pages remains accessible in the DOM structure without CSS styling. The evidence shows content elements that are all structurally present in the HTML (headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, forms). The single case of CSS-controlled visibility (the tooltip with id="astuce-tls" using display:none) is additional content, not primary information. All primary visible information is conveyed through HTML structural elements that would remain readable when CSS is disabled.

Test 10.3.1 requires that information remains comprehensible when CSS is disabled—meaning the reading order (DOM order) must be logical. Examination of the DOM shows proper structural ordering: skip link, header with nav, main content with headings and sections, footer. The content flows in a natural reading order without CSS-dependent reordering via flexbox, grid, or positioning that would disrupt comprehension. Elements follow standard semantic HTML5 structure.

The accueil page violates 10.4.2 by blocking zoom via viewport meta tag, and violates 10.4.1 by truncating text at high zoom levels through fixed-height containers with overflow:hidden. Both tests fail.

findings.message: Viewport meta tag blocks user zoom: user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1 prevent zoom to 200%. Test 10.4.2 requires that 200% zoom must be possible for the entire text.

Text truncation at 200% zoom: CSS applies overflow:hidden and white-space:nowrap to this paragraph, causing loss of content when text is enlarged (test 10.4.1). The text 'Le réseau Orbit compte douze points de présence répartis sur quatre continents, et une latence médiane inférieure à trente millisecondes' will be cut off.

entries.justification: Test 10.5.1 and 10.5.2 require that when color is declared for text, background color must also be declared (and vice versa). The evidence shows the accueil page paragraph at line 59 with both color (#bbbbbb) and background-color (#ffffff) properly declared together: style="color:#bbbbbb;background:#ffffff". This satisfies both tests—text color is accompanied by background color and vice versa.

The stylesheet explicitly removes text-decoration from links (line 73: 'text-decoration: none') and sets 'font-weight: inherit', removing all visual indicators except color. While the 3.95:1 contrast ratio meets the threshold, test 10.6.1 requires that links distinguished solely by color must also have 'une indication visuelle au survol autre qu'un changement de couleur' (visual indication on hover other than color change) and 'une indication visuelle au focus autre qu'un changement de couleur' (visual indication on focus other than color change). No such :hover or :focus rules exist in the stylesheet. The page shows multiple instances of this pattern across all navigation and content links.

findings.message: Links in text blocks (p and li elements) are distinguished only by color with no underline, border, or font weight change. The stylesheet defines no hover or focus pseudo-classes to provide additional visual indication beyond color change.

entries.justification: Test 10.8.1 requires that hidden content (including content controlled by the disabled attribute) must either: (1) have vocation to be ignored by assistive technologies, OR (2) be made restituable by user action on a preceding element or by focus repositioning. The disabled fieldset at line 125-131 contains a 'Récapitulatif' (summary) section with read-only display values. When a fieldset is disabled, the W3C specification states that all form controls are disabled, and this typically results in the content being ignored or unavailable to assistive technologies. The structure provides no preceding interactive element (button, link) that would trigger display of this content, nor any mechanism to make it available via keyboard or pointer action.

findings.snippet:
<fieldset disabled="">
  <legend>Récapitulatif</legend>
  <label for="recap-societe">Société</label>
  <input id="recap-societe" type="text" value="Orbit">
  <label for="recap-siret">SIRET</label>
  <input id="recap-siret" type="text" value="00000000000000">
</fieldset>
findings.message: A fieldset with the disabled attribute wraps read-only summary fields. When a fieldset is disabled, all form controls within it are also disabled and typically not exposed to assistive technologies. No user action (keyboard, pointer, or focus) can make this disabled content accessible.

entries.justification: The only evidence presented is a comment in the HTML source code (tests/fixtures/realworld/index.html:2) noting that the site is a 'jeu d'essai de rappel' (test/recall game) where defects are 'planted'. This comment is metadata about the test site itself, not evidence of information conveyed to end users through form, size, or position. No actual content in the rendered pages conveys information solely through form, size, or position changes to users viewing the site's functional content.

This is metadata about the page structure, not evidence of user-facing information presented solely through form, size, or position. No actual content instances were identified where information is conveyed solely by form, size, or position without alternative text or semantic alternatives.

entries.justification: Test 10.11.1 requires that when content with horizontal text flow is displayed in a 320px wide window, all information and functionality must remain available without horizontal scrolling (except for specified exceptions like tables, images, games, presentations, and interfaces requiring two-dimensional manipulation). The stylesheet defines 'min-width: 1200px' on the body, which prevents content from reflowing at 320px. Evidence from multiple pages (accueil, cadres-html, contact-html, documents-html, medias-html, mentions-legales-html, plan-html, recherche-html, tarifs-html) shows 'Horizontal scrolling at 320px width — content does not reflow.' This is a systematic failure across all 10 pages in the audit.

findings.message: The body element has 'min-width: 1200px' which forces a minimum width of 1200 pixels. At the required 320px viewport width, this constraint forces horizontal scrolling because the content cannot reflow to fit the narrower viewport.

entries.justification: Test 10.12.1 requires that text remains readable when display is modified with increased text spacing: line-height up to 1.5× font size, paragraph bottom margin up to 2× font size, letter-spacing up to 0.12× font size, and word-spacing up to 0.16× font size. The .entrefilet CSS rule uses a fixed height (20px) with overflow:hidden, which will truncate content when spacing increases. The page contains a paragraph with class='entrefilet' at accueil (line 111): 'Le réseau Orbit compte douze points de présence répartis sur quatre continents, et une latence médiane inférieure à trente millisecondes.' When text spacing is applied per the test methodology, this content becomes truncated and unreadable.

findings.message: The .entrefilet class applies a fixed height of 20px with overflow: hidden and white-space: nowrap. When text spacing properties are increased (line-height, letter-spacing, word-spacing, or paragraph margins), the fixed height will cause text to overflow and be clipped by the overflow:hidden rule.

The tooltip content (aria-describedby #astuce-tls) does not close when the Escape key is pressed. According to test 10.13.1, users must be able to hide additional content appearing on hover/focus without moving the focus or pointer. The Escape key handler is not implemented.

The stylesheet at /styles.css uses :hover pseudo-class to reveal the tooltip (display:none by default, display:block on :hover), but there is no :focus or :focus-within equivalent. This violates test 10.14.1 which requires that additional CSS content appearing on hover must also appear on keyboard activation or focus.
Input field has no label, title, or aria-label - violates 11.1.1
Input field labeled only by placeholder attribute, not a proper label per RGAA definition - violates 11.1.1 and 11.1.3
Input field labeled only by title attribute; title is not reliably conveyed (hover-only) - violates 11.1.3
Label references non-existent field 'champ-supprime' - violates 11.1.2
Select element is empty (no options) - violates 11.1.1
Form field has two labels with same 'for' attribute creating ambiguity - violates 11.1.2
Image input button has no alt text or aria-label - violates 11.1.1

entries.justification: All existing proper form field labels (using <label> elements with 'for' attributes, aria-label, or aria-labelledby) that appear in the evidence are semantically pertinent and relevant to their associated fields. Examples include 'Adresse e-mail de secours', 'Adresse e-mail de facturation', 'Téléphone', 'Pays', 'Offre concernée', 'Devise', 'Début de la migration', 'Fin souhaitée', 'Mot de passe du compte', 'SIRET', 'Société', and 'Tapez SUPPRIMER pour confirmer'. These labels accurately convey the purpose and function of their respective fields. The evidence does not show any cases where a properly associated label is irrelevant or vague. (Note: Issues with missing or improperly associated labels are 11.1 violations, not 11.2.)

It accurately conveys the nature of the contained form fields. While many groups lack legends (a 11.6 issue), the existing legend satisfies test 11.7.1 by being relevant and descriptive.

The SIRET field error message 'Le SIRET doit comporter quatorze chiffres' provides format specification but does not provide an explicit example value (such as a sample SIRET number like '12345678901234'). Test 11.11.2 requires that examples of expected values be suggested when necessary.

Email field collecting user data lacks autocomplete attribute

entries.justification: The site provides three navigation mechanisms satisfying test 12.1.1: (1) main navigation menu with multiple links present on most pages (Navigation principale), (2) a dedicated sitemap page (plan du site) with links to site pages, and (3) a search form on the recherche page. This satisfies the requirement for at least two of these three systems.

Navigation elements maintain consistent visual and source positioning across pages. The header contains the main navigation (nav aria-label="Navigation principale") in the same location and order on multiple pages (accueil, contact-html, tarifs-html, etc.). Footer navigation appears consistently positioned at the end with the same relative order. Test 12.2.1 requirements for visual consistency and code order consistency are met.

The sitemap page (plan du site) contains a navigation element with links to eight main pages of the site (Accueil, Tarifs, Contact, Médias, Intégrations, Documents, Recherche, Mentions légales). The links use proper href attributes with correct URL patterns matching page labels. Tests 12.3.1 (representative architecture), 12.3.2 (functional links), and 12.3.3 (links point to correct pages) are satisfied.

The plan du site is not accessible via identical functionality across the page set. It is present as a header link on accueil, as a footer link on several pages (cadres-html, contact-html, tarifs-html), but completely absent from the footer of the plan page itself and the recherche page. Test 12.4.1 requires the means of access to be identical; test 12.4.2 requires it to be at the same location in presentation. Neither condition is met.

findings.snippet: Plan du site link in header on accueil page
findings.message: The plan du site is accessible via header navigation on accueil page but not consistently on other pages

findings.snippet: Footer on plan-html page contains only copyright, no plan du site link back
findings.message: Plan du site page itself has no footer link back to maintain consistency - violates identical functionality requirement
Recherche page footer is empty with no plan du site link, unlike other pages with footer navigation

The search engine functionality is located in the middle of the main content on the recherche page (form at line 29 of /recherche.html) but appears in the header on all other pages. Test 12.5.2 requires that the search functionality is situated at the same place in the presentation across pages. Test 12.5.3 requires it appears in the same relative order in the code source.

The page has a header with 9 navigation links but no <nav> landmark or role="navigation". According to test 12.6.1, the navigation zone must have a landmark role (like <nav>) or another method to be distinguished and reached (title, hide button, skip link, or quick access link).

This page has no <main> landmark. The main content area is not identified. According to test 12.6.1, the main content zone must have a landmark (like <main>), a title, a hide button, a skip link, or a quick access link.

Multiple navigation landmarks exist on this page without aria-label or aria-labelledby to distinguish them. According to test 12.6.1, multiple navigational zones must be identifiable by having unique labels or roles.
The skip link targets #principal but the main element has id="contenu" (not id="principal"). The skip link is non-functional. According to test 12.7.2, the skip link must be functional.

entries.justification: The positive tabindex values (1 and 3) force a tab order that is incoherent with the DOM structure. In the source order, the input appears before the button, but the tabindex values cause the button to receive focus first (tabindex="1"), then the input (tabindex="3"). This violates test 12.8.1 which requires coherent tab order relative to content.

findings.message: Submit button has tabindex="1" which gives it first focus position despite appearing after input in DOM
Search input has tabindex="3" which forces it to receive focus after button (tabindex="1") - reverses natural DOM order

entries.justification: Test 12.9.1 requires that it be possible to reach the next or previous focusable element with Tab, or that the user is informed of an alternative mechanism. This input field explicitly prevents Tab from leaving (event.preventDefault()) and forces focus back to itself with this.focus(). This creates an inescapable keyboard trap that violates the core requirement.

findings.snippet: <input id="confirmation" name="confirmation" type="text" onkeydown="if (event.key === 'Tab') { event.preventDefault(); this.focus(); }">
findings.message: Input field intercepts Tab key with preventDefault() and refocuses itself, creating an explicit keyboard trap

entries.justification: No evidence was collected for single-key shortcuts in the audited scope. The audit search found no keyboard shortcuts using only a single key (letters, numbers, punctuation, or symbols) that require management. The criterion does not apply when no such shortcuts are present in the site.

Test 12.11.1 requires that additional content appearing on component interaction be reachable by keyboard when it contains interactive components. The tooltip on accueil page contains text that appears only on pointer hover (styles.css shows only .astuce:hover .astuce-contenu selector without :focus-within equivalent). When a keyboard user focuses the button, the tooltip content is not revealed, making it unreachable. This violates the test requirement for keyboard accessibility of additional content.

findings.message: Button that triggers tooltip content via aria-describedby
Tooltip content is only visible on :hover according to styles.css line 129 (.astuce:hover .astuce-contenu), not on :focus-within - not keyboard accessible

entries.justification: The meta refresh with 3600-second delay does not meet any of the four conditions specified in test 13.1.1. The user cannot control the refresh, cannot extend the limit, receives no warning, and the 1-hour limit is significantly less than the 20-hour minimum required.

findings.message: The meta refresh element has a 3600-second (1-hour) delay but does not allow user control of the refresh rate. Test 13.1.1 requires that refresh mechanisms must allow users to either: (1) stop/restart the refresh, (2) extend the limit 10x, (3) receive a 20-second warning before refresh occurs, or (4) have a limit of 20+ hours. Since the delay is 1 hour (less than 20 hours) and none of the other control mechanisms are present, this violates the criterion.

entries.justification: Le critère 13.2 s'adresse spécifiquement à « l'ouverture d'une nouvelle fenêtre » (pop-up, pop-under, new window/tab). La meta refresh est un mécanisme de redirection dans la même fenêtre, pas l'ouverture d'une nouvelle fenêtre. Cette problématique relève du critère 13.1 (limite de temps), non de 13.2. Le critère 13.2 est hors de portée pour ce type de contenu.

Le test 13.3.1 exige pour chaque document bureautique en téléchargement une de ces trois conditions : (1) le document est compatible avec l'accessibilité, (2) il existe une version alternative en téléchargement compatible, ou (3) il existe une version alternative en HTML. Les quatre liens présentent uniquement des fichiers bureautiques (PDF, DOCX, XLSX) sans indication visible d'alternatives accessibles ou versions HTML alternatives. Le balisage HTML ne montre aucun lien adjacent vers une version alternative ou une marque d'accessibilité.

findings.message: Lien de téléchargement PDF sans indication de version accessible ou alternative en HTML.
Lien de téléchargement DOCX sans indication de version accessible ou alternative.
Lien de téléchargement XLSX sans indication de version accessible ou alternative.
Lien de téléchargement PDF sans indication de version accessible ou alternative.

entries.justification: Le critère 13.4 ne s'applique que « pour chaque document bureautique ayant une version accessible ». Selon la conclusion du critère 13.3, aucune version accessible n'est proposée pour ces documents. Le critère 13.4 est donc hors de portée : il présuppose l'existence de versions accessibles qui font défaut.

Le critère 13.5 s'applique spécifiquement à « chaque contenu cryptique (art ASCII, émoticône, syntaxe cryptique) ». Les éléments présentés (images, canvas, object, SVG) sont des médias ou des éléments graphiques qui ont des problèmes d'accessibilité différents (absence d'alt, d'accessible name), mais ne constituent pas du « contenu cryptique » au sens du critère. Le contenu cryptique désigne des textes/symboles utilisés de façon non évidente (art ASCII, émoticônes, syntaxe de programmation). Les images et graphiques ne relèvent pas de cette catégorie pour le test 13.5. Ces éléments sont couverts par d'autres critères (notamment 1.1 pour les images).

citations.snippet: <svg viewBox="0 0 100 40"><rect x="0" y="10" width="20" height="30"></rect><rect x="30" y="4" width="20" height="36"></rect></svg>

entries.justification: Le critère 13.6 évalue la pertinence des alternatives pour « contenu cryptique (art ASCII, émoticône, syntaxe cryptique) ». Comme le critère 13.5, il ne s'applique que au contenu cryptique au sens strict. Les éléments présentés (images, canvas, object, SVG) ne constituent pas du contenu cryptique pour le test 13.6. Le critère est hors de portée pour ce type de contenu.

citations.snippet: <svg viewBox="0 0 100 40"><rect x="0" y="10" width="20" height="30"></rect><rect x="30" y="4" width="20" height="36"></rect></svg>

entries.justification: The evidence identifies various media elements (img, svg, canvas, object, video) in the captured pages but does not provide information about whether they actually cause flashing or rapid brightness changes. The DOM shows static image file references with no CSS animations visible in styles.json. However, a single static screenshot cannot demonstrate whether any element actually flashes over time. To determine if these elements meet the criterion's threshold of <3 flashes/second or <21824 pixels cumulative area, one would need to observe the rendered page over time or analyze any animation code. The captured files do not provide sufficient evidence to settle whether flashing actually occurs.

The marquee element is moving/blinking content that scrolls indefinitely with no user control, violating test 13.8.2. The autoplay audio element lacks controls to stop/pause the sound, violating test 13.8.1. Neither element meets any of the four control conditions required by the criterion.

findings.snippet: <marquee>Maintenance planifiée le 12 septembre de 2 h à 4 h.</marquee>
findings.message: The marquee element displays moving text that scrolls automatically with no user control mechanism. Test 13.8.2 requires that automatically triggered blinking/moving content must either: (1) have a duration ≤5 seconds, (2) allow the user to pause and restart, (3) allow the user to hide and show the content, or (4) allow viewing the complete information without motion. This marquee has no visible duration limit (scrolls indefinitely), no pause button, no hide/show mechanism, and no static alternative text. It violates all conditions.

The audio element has the autoplay attribute set but lacks the controls attribute, meaning audio plays automatically without any user control to pause, stop, or adjust volume. Test 13.8.1 requires that auto-triggered moving/auto-updating content must either: (1) have duration ≤5 seconds, (2) allow pause/restart, (3) allow hide/show, or (4) allow viewing information without motion. Without visible controls and given that the audio file ('journal-incidents.mp3') is unlikely to be ≤5 seconds, this fails the criterion's requirements.

entries.justification: La présence de la règle media query qui pivote le document HTML en mode portrait empêche la consultation en mode portrait. Cela viole le premier point du test 13.9.1 : 'La consultation est possible quel que soit le mode d'orientation de l'écran'. Cette règle s'applique à toutes les 9 pages capturées (accueil, cadres-html, contact-html, documents-html, medias-html, mentions-legales-html, plan-html, recherche-html, tarifs-html) qui partagent le même fichier CSS.

findings.message: La règle CSS force une rotation de 90° en mode portrait, verrouillant le contenu à l'orientation paysage. Les utilisateurs en mode portrait ne peuvent pas consulter le contenu sans rotation forcée, violant le test 13.9.1.

entries.justification: Le critère 13.10 s'applique aux fonctionnalités utilisant des gestes complexes (multi-point touch : 13.10.1, ou gestes basés sur une trajectoire : 13.10.2). L'évidence présentée est un simple div avec onclick, qui est un événement pointer simple, pas un geste complexe. Aucune fonctionnalité multi-point ou basée sur une trajectoire n'est présente sur la page. La page ne contient pas les types de gestures qu'évalue ce critère.

L'événement onclick se déclenche sur l'événement JavaScript 'click', qui se produit après mouseup/touchend (au relâchement). Le test 13.11.1 condition 1 est satisfait : 'L'action est déclenchée au moment où le dispositif de pointage est relâché ou relevé'. Cette implémentation permet à l'utilisateur d'annuler l'action en glissant son pointeur en dehors de l'élément avant de relâcher.

Le critère 13.12 s'applique aux fonctionnalités disponibles en bougeant l'appareil (13.12.1) ou en faisant un geste en direction de l'appareil (13.12.2), ainsi qu'à la possibilité de désactiver la détection du mouvement (13.12.3). L'évidence présentée est un simple div avec onclick, qui est un événement pointer standard non lié à aucune détection de mouvement d'appareil. Aucune fonctionnalité utilisant des capteurs d'appareil n'est présente sur la page.
